subject.title: fix(scripts): bound gh-read GitHub CLI execution

question: Should `scripts/gh-read` impose a two-minute timeout on all existing commands by default, including long-lived reads that previously had no deadline?
rationale: The code can enforce a finite deadline mechanically, but only maintainers can decide whether changing existing unattended long-running workflows is an acceptable repository-automation contract or whether callers need a compatibility-preserving migration path.

options.title: Preserve existing long-lived callers
options.body: Provide an explicit caller-facing timeout contract or migration path that lets established long-lived reads retain their behavior while bounding ordinary operations.

options.title: Adopt the breaking two-minute default
options.body: Accept that existing commands exceeding two minutes must set `OPENCLAW_GH_READ_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`, and document the operator upgrade requirement prominently.

options.title: Narrow the wrapper scope
options.body: Apply a finite deadline only to known finite `gh-read` operations and keep long-lived command support outside this wrapper.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing long-lived callers
recommendation.body: Provide an explicit caller-facing timeout contract or migration path that lets established long-lived reads retain their behavior while bounding ordinary operations.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent timeout work is the strongest available evidence of recent ownership of the scripts timeout pattern.
